- File: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh
  Location: line 112 (`if [ "${ENABLED}" = "false" ]; then`)
  Issue: Gate is case-sensitive; only exact lowercase `"false"` disables. Under the old `!= "true"` logic, any non-`"true"` value (including `"FALSE"`, `"False"`, `"no"`, `"0"`) would have disabled triage. Now those values will silently enable triage. An admin intending to disable who enters `CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_ENABLED=FALSE` would not see their intent honored, and would incur unexpected API/model costs.
  Suggested minimal fix: Use lowercase parameter expansion for case-insensitive comparison: `if [ "${ENABLED,,}" = "false" ]; then`. One line change.
  Estimated lines changed: 1
